# M9 sensitivity study: interleaving vs A/B

**All users are simulated** (click models below, relevance from TREC DL 2019+2020 graded qrels). No number here is user traffic. Generated by `scripts/m9_sensitivity.py`; raw data in `sensitivity.json`.

N80 = total query impressions for 80% power at two-sided p<0.05 **in the offline-correct direction** (A/B splits N in half). Pool of 2,000,000 simulated impressions per arm/method, 1000 trials per grid point, 20 grid points per decade. `*` = N80 above pool/10 (pool-limited). 'not reached' = power never reached 0.8 up to 1e8 (including when the metric favours the offline-worse ranker).

## Summary: how many more impressions A/B needs than team-draft interleaving

## A/A false-positive rate (fresh simulation per trial, no pool)

Ranker `anserini-bm25-default` against itself, N=2000 impressions per trial, 1000 trials, alpha=0.05. KS = p-value of a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of p-value uniformity (the sign test is discrete, so its p-values are conservative, not uniform).
